**Finding submitted: WARRANTY — deviation (fallback-level cure).**

What I found across the document:
- **§9(b) (p0032–p0041)** carries Kubient's express warranties: non-infringement, performance "in all material respects to industry standards", security/best practices, no malicious code (p0036), compliance with applicable Laws (p0041), and services "free from errors that materially affect their utility".
- **§13 Disclaimer (p0062)** opens "Except as expressly set forth herein" and carves out "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement", so the "as is" language does **not** swallow the express warranties — no disclaimer carve-out edit was needed.
- Targeted searches for documentation/conformance, refund, remedy, re-performance and day-periods returned **nothing**: there is no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no warranty duration, and **no warranty remedy anywhere** in the Agreement.

Because two material fallback terms (documentation conformance period for software, 30-day services period) and both remedy elements are absent, the clause fails fallback. I inserted a single new sub-clause (xii) after p0041 giving 90 days for the Service, Auction Platform and deliverables against documentation, 30 days for services against the Agreement's requirements, with repair/replacement or refund of fees paid — all four fallback elements in one operation, leaving the existing ongoing warranties untouched so no protection is narrowed. The preferred 12-month period and "professional and workmanlike" wording are flagged in the rationale as an upgrade ask, not redlined.
